title: Private VPC Discovery - Solaris Retail
summary: Initial discovery for Solaris Retail exploring Redwood Private (VPC) deployment. Customer requires cross-account VPC peering or PrivateLink, corporate firewall egress IPs, AWS region constraints (eu-west-1 requirement), SOC2/KMS concerns, and integration with Okta SSO. Next steps: share network guide, security package, and schedule technical deep dive and bench run.
action_items: Ravi Patel - draft network diagram of proposed private endpoint flow and share with Maya - 2026-03-20
Casey Nguyen - send Redwood security package (SOC 2, encryption, KMS integration doc) - 2026-03-18
Maya Chen - provide current VPC CIDR ranges and peering constraints + proxy/NAT details - 2026-03-19
Omar Ruiz - confirm data residency and retention policy questions via email - 2026-03-18
next_steps: Schedule SE deep-dive to run network diagram review and walk routing tables (proposed: 2026-03-22)
Share proof-of-concept (PoC) scope and pricing estimate for dedicated capacity + private VPC option
Run short benchmark with sample workload in eu-west-1 (if access approved)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 15:00 PST / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Casey (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Jordan (Solaris CTO), Maya (Infra), Omar (Sec), Hannah (Product)
Links shared: 1) Redwood private deployment one-pager (link), 2) security pack (link), 3) sample network diagram (link)

[00:00] Casey: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear ok?
[00:05] Jordan: yep yep hearing you, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to get into the networking details for a private deployment, so high level first then we can dig into routing and firewall stuff.
[00:17] Casey: perfect, yeah so today we'll cover how Redwood Private works with VPC peering and private endpoints, options for cross-account setup, and also what the traffic egress looks like, any region constraints. ravi and lena will cover a lot of the infra details.
[00:30] Ravi: hi all, quick caveat, my audio is a bit rough, so apologies if i cut out. quick question for you jordan - what's driving private over hosted? is it regulation, data residency, or just wanting VPC isolation?
[00:42] Jordan: mostly data residency and corporate policy. we have customers in EU and need to host in eu-west-1. also security insists on egress IP allowlisting and we want to avoid internet facing endpoints.
[00:55] Maya: and on top of that we run in multiple accounts, we prefer cross-account peering or PrivateLink to avoid opening up public endpoints. we also have strict route table and nat gateway policies.
[01:05] Ravi: got it. ok so options: 1) VPC peering directly from customer VPC to Redwood-managed VPC (cross-account peering), 2) AWS PrivateLink / interface VPC endpoints that we create into your account, or 3) a hybrid using Transit Gateway if scale demands. each has tradeoffs.
[01:23] Lena: i'll add that PrivateLink gives you more controlled egress since traffic stays on AWS backbone and you can maintain your own NAT/egress ips, whereas peering is simpler but requires careful route table management.
[01:35] Omar: question: for PrivateLink, do we need to accept interface endpoints in our account or does Redwood create them? also how does auth work?
[01:43] Ravi: good q - we typically offer two modes. for PrivateLink we can either publish a service and you create an interface endpoint in your account (you accept the endpoint and pay endpoint charges), or if customers prefer we can set up cross-account endpoints with service consumer arrangement. auth is still bearer token over TLS; we can also restrict via security group rules on the endpoint.
[02:03] Jordan: what about IP allowlisting? security wants static egress IPs so firewalls can allowlist, we can't have ephemeral addresses.
[02:11] Casey: on Redwood Private we can provide a set of egress ips from our nat egress or we can terminate in your VPC so all outbound to external services go through your nat. so two patterns: bring-your-own-egress or Redwood egress with fixed ips.
[02:26] Maya: we prefer bringing our own egress so we can monitor and route through our proxies. do you support routing all model traffic into a customer-managed Egress VPC?
[02:35] Ravi: yes, if we peer into your VPC you can control outbound traffic. with PrivateLink you still manage egress for connections initiated from your side. one gotcha is if Redwood needs to reach back for logs or control plane hooks, that traffic might originate from Redwood-managed infrastructure unless you opt for fully customer-hosted data plane.
[02:52] Jordan: that leads to the question of network connectivity for model updates or KV cache syncs - do those cross the peering link?
[03:00] Lena: model artifacts are typically pulled from a model store in the region. for Private deployments we can either stage the model in your account's S3 (you can opt to host artifacts) or we can pull them across a peering link. hosting in your S3 is recommended for strict data controls.
[03:15] Maya: ok if we host artifacts in our S3, does Redwood need cross-account IAM roles?
[03:21] Ravi: yes we can have an IAM role in your account that Redwood assumes for model pulls. we provide a minimal policy. alternatively we can do signed URLs if you prefer not to manage roles.
[03:31] Omar: encryption at rest and KMS - our policy mandates using our KMS keys for everything. is that supported?
[03:37] Casey: we support CMKs via cross-account KMS grants in the private deployment. you can bring-your-own-key so data at rest in your S3 uses your CMK. for Redwood-managed storage we use our own keys but will negotiate BYOK for private installs.
[03:52] Jordan: region constraints — we need eu-west-1 only for PII. do you support Private deployments in that region?
[03:59] Ravi: yes we support eu-west-1; we have capacity but we recommend checking for dedicated capacity availability. for hosted we have multi-region options but for dedicated/private we can spin up capacity in the specific region—subject to lead time and reserved capacity commitments.
[04:16] Maya: what's the typical lead time to get a private VPC deployment up in a new region?
[04:20] Lena: usually 2-4 weeks for standard config if capacity available; if you need reserved GPUs and dedicated pools could be 4-8 weeks based on procurement.
[04:29] Jordan: pricing question — is there a premium for Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:34] Casey: yes a private, single-tenant VPC option typically has platform and ops fees plus potential network egress handling. dedicated (shared network but dedicated GPU pools) is between hosted and private. we'll send a pricing band in the follow up.
[04:47] Omar: audit logs and compliance — can we pull CloudTrail logs or do you provide an audit export?
[04:52] Ravi: we can integrate with your logging. options: push logs to your S3 via cross-account delivery, or we can provide log exports. we support syslog/forwarding and can enable detailed request-level audit logs for compliance.
[05:05] Maya: on firewall rules, we need source IPs for the service endpoints. if you do PrivateLink, we can lock SGs to the endpoint. with peering we need to allow the Redwood VPC CIDR. what's your recommended pattern?
[05:16] Ravi: recommended for strict security is PrivateLink with interface endpoints plus security group restrictions. peering is fine for internal-only traffic but harder to lock down origin IPs unless we control egress IPs.
[05:29] Jordan: transit gateway — if we have many accounts, is that supported?
[05:33] Lena: yes we can attach to Transit Gateway. we've done setups where the customer TGW handles routing to multiple accounts and we peer/attach there. note that costs and complexity increase but it scales nicely.
[05:45] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry.
[05:50] Omar: what about latency and token throughput across peering? we need to guarantee sub-200ms p95 for short prompts.
[05:59] Ravi: latency depends on model size and sequence lengths; network adds a small delta. for eu-west-1 hosting in-region you should see minimal network latencies. for p95 under 200ms you'd likely pick an optimized quantized model and dedicated instance type; we can run benchmarks during PoC.
[06:17] Maya: can we run a benchmark behind our NAT so we can measure egress and firewall behavior?
[06:22] Casey: yes, we can do a bench run that originates from your VPC using interface endpoints or peering. we'll need your network team to open the endpoints and share CIDRs.
[06:34] Jordan: ok great. one more: SSO / RBAC integration — okta is our identity provider. how do you integrate?
[06:41] Lena: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management, and RBAC at the tenant and project level. for Private we can integrate with your IdP over SAML and use SCIM for provisioning.
[06:52] Omar: retention and data access — we need guarantees that user data isn't stored beyond session unless explicitly persisted. can you map that?
[06:58] Casey: yes in private deployments you control data retention policy. we can turn off transcript retention on the Redwood side and ensure logs are forwarded to your logging. we'll document exact retention options in the security pack.
[07:10] Maya: any gotchas with Kubernetes networking if we host in our account?
[07:15] Ravi: if you host the data plane in your k8s cluster, be mindful of KV cache size and ephemeral storage for models; networking-wise you'll want sufficient ENI limits and adjust pod density per GPU. we've seen customers forget ip-per-pod quotas and then routes get messy.
[07:31] Jordan: who will maintain OS patches and runtime updates in private?
[07:36] Lena: two modes: fully-managed by Redwood (we push updates) or you manage OS/runtime in your environment. for compliance some customers prefer that we only manage the application layer while ops team handles host patching.
[07:50] Casey: ok we're about 45 minutes in — want to surface the key takeaways and next steps.
[07:55] Jordan: go ahead.
[07:57] Casey: recap: Solaris needs eu-west-1 private deployment with egress via customer NAT, static egress IPs, PrivateLink preferred for strict security but peering supported, BYOK for S3/KMS, Okta SAML SCIM for SSO, and audit log forwarding. next: we'll share security package, draft network diagram, and schedule SE deep-dive and bench.
[08:17] Jordan: that's accurate. also please include pricing ranges and what reserved capacity lead times look like.
[08:24] Casey: will do. thanks everyone.
[08:28] Maya: thanks, we'll send the VPC cidrs and a brief network inventory by tomorrow.
[08:33] Omar: i'll follow up on data retention questions via email.
[08:36] Casey: great. end of call.
